name: Glovebox: Car Service Log
subtitle: MOT & Oil Change Reminders
promotionalText: Every service, MOT and oil change your car has had, on your phone. No account, no server, nothing to sync and nothing to lose. CSV export is free for everyone.
description:
Your service history, kept for good. On your phone, not on somebody else's server.

Most car maintenance apps ask you to make an account, sync to a server and hope nothing breaks. One bad login and years of service history are gone. Glovebox works the other way round: no account, no server, nothing to sync. Every oil change, tyre rotation and MOT you log stays on your phone.

WHAT IT DOES
- Log oil changes, tyre rotations, brakes, filters, coolant, the MOT and anything else you care to type in, for as many cars as you run
- Get a reminder the day the next one is due, by date or by mileage, whichever comes first
- Log an MOT and the next one is set a year ahead, so the date you cannot legally miss sits on the phone rather than in your head
- See a car's whole service history on one screen
- Export the lot to CSV whenever you want. Export is free for everyone and never sits behind the subscription

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT
No account. No login. No server. No sync to break. Your service history cannot vanish, because there is nothing for it to vanish from. It is on the phone, the way the paper service book used to live in the glovebox.

BUILT FOR PEOPLE WHO KEEP THEIR CARS
- Every car you own, each with its own schedule and its own mileage
- Your own intervals for oil changes, tyre rotations, brake pads, air and cabin filters, coolant and the rest
- Due by date or due by mileage, whichever lands first
- Road tax, cambelt, air-con service: anything that comes round again can go in with an interval of your own
- Dark, glare-friendly screens, meant to be read on a driveway or standing at a garage counter

WHO IT IS FOR
Daily drivers, DIY mechanics, people running an older car on a budget, and anyone who will eventually sell or part-exchange. A dated, complete service history is the part of a used car a buyer will actually pay for; "I'm sure that was done" is not. Keep it in one searchable log instead of a folder of paper receipts and a shoebox of MOT certificates.

WHAT IT IS NOT
It does not plug into the OBD port, read your engine, look up your registration or book you in anywhere. It keeps the record, properly, and reminds you. That is the whole job.

Free for one car. Glovebox Pro adds room for the rest of your cars and your own service intervals. Export stays free, for everyone.

notes.reasoning: The harvest splits into four British intents and the indexed fields cover all four without spending a word twice. NAME takes the highest-volume prefix in the harvest, "car" (car service history, car logbook, car maintenance, car service book), plus "service" and "log". SUBTITLE takes what the name cannot reach: MOT and the oil-change reminder cluster (mot reminder, car mot reminder, oil change reminder, car maintenance reminders). MOT earns a subtitle slot rather than a keyword slot because it is the only search term in this market with a hard legal deadline behind it and the app names the test the way owners do. KEYWORDS carry only words used nowhere else, chosen to recombine with the name and subtitle: maintenance, history, book and logbook rebuild "car service history", "digital service book", "my service book", "car maintenance book", "car logbook", "mileage logbook" and "MOT history"; then mileage, odometer, vehicle, repair, tyre, brakes, records, tax (Road Tax is a real service type in the UK build), tracker and van. Deliberately left out: "garage", because the harvest proves the word is dead in this storefront (the garage log seed returned GarageBand, garage clothing, ringtones and limited companies) and because the UK build renames the vehicle list to "My cars" for exactly that reason, keeping "garage" for the workshop sense only, which the description follows; "reg check" and "registration search", a DVLA-lookup intent the app deliberately does not serve and which the WHAT IT IS NOT section explicitly disclaims; and everything metric, since the UK reads miles and the listing says mileage throughout. Spelling and framing are British: tyre, air-con, cambelt, part-exchange, MOT certificates, garage counter, "quote" thinking rather than US flipping. Supplied from market knowledge rather than from the harvest, so a reviewer knows which is judgement: the annual MOT cadence and its legal weight; cambelt, air-con service and road tax as the recurring items a UK owner actually tracks; part-exchange as the resale framing; and the keyword fillers "van" and "tracker", which the harvest supports only indirectly (mileage tracker, car maintenance tracker - mpg) and not at all for van. The harvest records autocomplete presence, not volume, so the relative weighting of "mot reminder" against "car service history" is inference rather than measurement.
